the sheet, the lesson, the save
A post hand walks under three rows on the same WORK_ORDERS table — `MUSTER.POST.rows = hours · training · keep` — read from the same `n.orders` store by the same `ordersOf`.

THE HOURS: round the clock, DAYS or NIGHTS — the shift clock only ticks in the hours the hand keeps, so a days hand rests at night with the clock held (the plate says *resting — the round keeps its hours*), and the lamp-lit round pays the town one appreciation more per shift because a town that sleeps easier thanks the hand that walks it.

figure.note: the row reads nights 1, round the clock 0; a lamp-lit shift pays 2 where a round-the-clock shift pays 1

clauses.text: THE TRAINING: the round's own verb, or CROSS-TRAIN — half the lesson to the round's verb and half to the hand's weakest skill, the note naming which.

figure.note: cross-trained, Footwork takes half the round's lesson (to 0.01) and Lumenistry, at nought, the rest

clauses.text: THE KEEP: wages from the bank as before, or THE TOWN'S TABLE — no provision drawn, two rations off the town's own shelf each shift, half the thanks; at the floor (ten rations) the round STALLS and the roll says the table is bare, exactly as an unpaid round stalls.

figure.record: two rations … half the thanks; at the floor (ten rations)
figure.note: the row reads table 2, ×0.5 and a floor of 10; with the shelf at 11 the round stalls with nothing taken

clauses.text: `NPC.workOf` hands the roll a fourth sheet kind, `post`, and the muster roll renders it with the hand's stripe: shifts, the skill trained with its progress, the appreciation given.
A lesson, THE POSTED ORDERS, walks on the first post order set.

Five causes join the sixteen: working in the greyfall (−2, read at the hand's own feet through `Systems.rainAt`), working nights (−2, a field hand at night or a post hand keeping nights), far from home (−1, a route or a chain past 2.4 km from the town), a town that thanks them (+1, HONOURED or better), fed at the town's table (+1).

figure.note: the rows read −2, −2, −1 beyond 2400, +1 at HONOURED, +1; out in the grey by night past 2.4 km the hauler sums −5, thanked −4

clauses.text: A stalled hand is still out there in it — the weather counts, paid or not.
Every band carries a WORK PACE the field speed reads (BRIGHT × 1.1, LOW × 0.85, DONE × 0.7)

figure.note: the bands' workMul read 1.1, 0.85, 0.7 and STEADY 1 (the rows' numbers; the field speed is not walked)

clauses.text: a field hand DONE for the minute comes in to the fire off the job with a mail naming every cause — the same law as a walker sitting down.
Unpaid, in the greyfall, at night, far from home is that minute.
The legend names all three.
THE LESSON: the posted orders (39 pages)
